rows.copy: A Rite in the Hill Country

rows.what: Date and place under the names

rows.copy: Two artists, one long December afternoon, and a circle of witnesses for an intimate wedding. Please join us.
Two of a kind, and a perfect kind of harmony

rows.what: One line in your own words (pull quote)
rows.copy: Established in 2009, they grew their love over seventeen years.
The first kiss was at The Showdown Saloon in 2009, and they have been together ever since. Seventeen years later, they are gathering the people they love to make it official and join two families.

rows.what: Schedule heading (the date in Roman numerals)

rows.copy: Tell your GPS “County Road,” not “Country Road.”
A buffet supper, a pour-your-own bar, cake, music, and the salt bowl ceremony. The sun sets at 5:31 PM; bring a layer.
About 25 minutes from the chapel. No shuttle; free parking on site and on the street.

rows.what: End of night schedule item 1 (time · detail)

rows.copy: Salt preserves. For as long as people have made promises, it has sealed them. At the reception, a bowl of salt will be waiting. Guests are encouraged to bring a symbolic or sentimental small item to place in the salt bowl to bless the marriage. Guests will be invited to voice their blessing, toast, words of wisdom, or share memories to honor of these two individuals and this marriage. We will start after guests have an opportunity to get a plate of food and a beverage.  The bowl will be out for the entire reception and all are welcomed to add to it at any time.
Please come in your most fabulous black ensemble.
Evenings may fall into the low 40s, and much of the day is spent outdoors. Bring layers for comfort.
We wish for everyone to be fully present during the ceremony. While we appreciate the gesture to document this day, we’ve got it taken care of with a talented photographer.

This is an intimate wedding and due to venue limitations, plus-ones only if named on the invitation. Please be advised there will be a pool on the property without a life guard on duty. White horse and small goat will be roaming on the property, please be respectful to the animals.
There are no room blocks; book wherever suits you. Some guests are staying at the Hyatt Place Austin - Cedar Park.
Hilton Garden Inn Cedar Park Austin
Also in Cedar Park, a few minutes from the reception.
On the San Gabriel River at Rivery Park, near the historic square. Closest to the chapel.
Where the other guests are staying. Practical, and between the two venues.
Driving back to San Marcos that night? It's about an hour south on I-35.
Between 3:30 and 3:50. We’ll be taking photos as guests arrive, and everyone is seated by 4:00.
Can I bring a plus-one or my children?
This is a small intimate wedding, and the venues have a limited headcount for guests: plus-ones only if they’re named on your invitation.
Gifts are welcomed but not expected. Guests are encouraged to bring a note or small item for the salt bowl.
The Lincoln Chapel and La Villa Rosa have free guest parking onsite. La Villa Rosa has free parking on site and on the street available.
The chapel has a gentle-slope entry and accessible restrooms about fifty feet away. Not every area of La Villa Rosa is wheelchair accessible; tell us what you need and we’ll make it work.
How do I get between venues?
By car, about 25 minutes. There’s no shuttle, so plan to drive or share a ride.

Casey Eickhoff, the Matron of Honor, can answer anything in our stead. Before the day, write to caseyisonit@gmail.com with “Meg + Ryan wedding” in the subject. On the day itself, email goes unchecked; Casey will share a number for texting with you directly.
Drinks are provided, and there’s a pour-your-own bar. If you have a drink of choice, you’re welcome to bring it.
There’s a pool at La Villa Rosa with no lifeguard on duty, and a white horse with a small goat roam the property. Please be kind to the animals.
